_comment: Aud3DObject's five default virtuals. NOT its constructor or destructor, and that is the whole
point: defining either of those makes MSVC emit its own ??_7Aud3DObject@@6B@, which would have
to be handed over by tools/asm_vtables.py. Defining only ordinary virtuals emits no table, so
the 1999 one stays in use and repoints itself to these definitions as their PROCs are stripped.
Update() is left out too, though it is a virtual and portable - keeping it in the assembly
leaves slot 3 reaching 1999 code while the rest reach C++, which is the mixed state that makes
porting a large class possible at all.
See the note at the top of aud3dobject.cpp before adding the constructor or destructor here:
the destructor's virtualness is contradicted between midtown2.map and the vftable itself.
